name: Determining When a Customer Could Rent a Car (Case 3)
description: Construct a program that determines whether a customer could rent a car based on the inputs that it receives from the car rental agent. Rental cars are available to licensed drivers who are either at least 21 years old or have a credit card with $10,000 or more of credit.

comments.content: We need to read and process the values that the car rental agent enters. To read the input values from the car rental agent, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the car rental agent to enter the customer's age in years.
We need to read the customer's age that the car rental agent enters and store it in a variable. We read the customer's age by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the car rental agent provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We prompt the car rental agent to enter whether the customer has driver's license.

We need to read whether the customer has driver's license and store it in a variable. We read whether the customer has driver's license by calling the nextBoolean() method because this input is a boolean. The variable hasLicense is true when the customer has driver's license, and false otherwise.
Note that if the car rental agent provides a non-boolean value, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., boolean.
We prompt the car rental agent to enter the customer's credit amount.

We need to read the customer's credit amount that the car rental agent enters and store it in a variable. We read the customer's credit amount by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the car rental agent provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the car rental agent in the rest of the program.

We need two conditions to determine whether the customer could rent a car. We use the && (and) operator to combine these conditions. The first condition is to test if the user has driver's license. The second condition is to test if the user is at least 21 years old or have the minimum credit amount.
The && operator yields the result true if both conditions are true while the || operator yields the result true if at least one of the conditions is true.
This statement prints true/false depending on whether the customer could rent a car. The printed value is followed by an end-of-line character in the end.
